I am 72 years old, and my wife and I have worked this 10.1 mu in Quzhou County for 20 years. I only went to primary school, but I know this land and this climate. We have a well, so I can pump water when the rains fail, but I watch the electricity bill carefully. With just the two of us left to do the work, I keep my methods simple and stick to what I know works. I don't try new tricks at my age.

My wheat is already in the ground from last October. I rotary tilled the maize stubble before sowing and bought improved seed from the township store — I don't save my own seed because the yield drops too much. I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, about 50 kg of the shop's usual 18-22-5 blend, before sowing. Now that spring is starting, I will topdress about 15 kg of urea per mu when the wheat greens up to help it tiller and fill the heads. I will irrigate three times in total for this wheat crop: the overwintering irrigation I already gave it, one at jointing, and one at grain filling. For chemicals, I will spray herbicide once, and I will watch for insects and disease — if I see aphids or the weather turns humid, I will spray once or twice more. I expect around 950 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

For maize, as soon as the wheat comes off the combine in early June, I will plant hybrid maize the same day. There is no time to waste in the wheat-maize double-cropping system, so I use no-tillage. Turning the soil takes too long and dries out the ground. I plant about 1.2 packages of hybrid seed per mu, usually Nongda or Denghai varieties that the dealer recommends. I put down one bag of high-nitrogen compound fertilizer per mu, around 28-6-6, at planting. I will irrigate twice: once right after sowing to get it to emerge, and once at the big trumpet stage. I will spray herbicide once, and insecticide two or three times for corn borer and other pests. Maize usually gives me about 1,150 kg per mu.
